newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania fears new flooding after Ukraine rain.
newsitem.headline: Romania fears new flooding after Ukraine rain.

text.p: Romanian officials on Wednesday trucked in drinking water and ordered mass vaccinations in flood-hit regions, warning of new danger ahead from heavy rains in neighbouring Ukraine.

The government acknowledged that weeks of rain, culminating in downpours and landslides last weekend, had placed added constraints on a revision of the 1997 budget and was damaging a forecast bumper grain crop.
Government officials said river levels, including the Romanian stretch of the Danube, were receding but more unstable weather was expected throughout August.
At least eight people have died in Romania, but the extent of the damage has been less dramatic than in Poland, Germany and the Czech Republic.
Nine were killed -- drowned or hit by lightning -- in the former Soviet republic of Moldova next door.
No deaths or major flooding were reported in Ukraine. But Romanian officials feared that rising water on the Prut River over the border would spill into Moldova and northern Romania.

"There could be problems on the upper reaches of the Prut, which has risen to flooding level due to rain in Ukraine," Octavian Ceachir, head of Romania's flood monitoring commission, said by telephone.
Health authorities warned against drinking tap water in stricken areas, especially in southern counties and around the major industrial city of Brasov in Transylvania.
Typhoid vaccine was sent to affected regions. Residents were told to report immediately any cases of diarrhoea.
"We will have to raise the price of water to consumers so much that it will become a luxury," Environment Minister Ioan Oltean told the independent Mediafax news agency.
He said budget cuts had forced his ministry to halt all work on flood prevention, including dike maintenance.
The Environment Ministry issued its first estimate of losses, not including the damage of the last few days, at the equivalent of nearly $110 million.
Thousands of homes have been damaged throughout the Balkan country of 22 million people.
Agriculture Minister Dinu Gavrilescu revised down to 6.9 million tonnes a predicted bumper wheat crop earlier estimated at 7.1 million.
